verdict: v7.1's ~215 units are buildable in ~22 dev-weeks of single-lane work, ~10 calendar weeks at the 6-chat concurrency PRISM actually runs. SFC GA is the near-term gate (~3.5 wk single-lane / ~2 calendar wk); Master Post GA lands ~wk 9-10; MS-PILOT phase-7 is per-machine, ~1.5-2 wk each after MS-TRAIN completes. Roadmap is realistic IF P0 stays serialized and the 415-engine MS3.5 wire-backlog is NOT pulled into the GA critical path.

velocity_anchor.source: git log: U-VIZ-* / U-WIRE-* batches run 6-12 units/commit, multi-commit/day; architectural units (SpindleCharacteristicEngine, ToolCatalogEngine, Master-Post skeleton) are 1-3/day each

summary.concurrency_assumption: 6 chats, but P0 work must serialize (shared dispatcher surface + 3way scrutiny gate) -> realistic parallelism factor ~2.2x not 6x

findings.title: MS0 (SFC, 61 units) is the long pole and over-weighted with P0 architectural units
findings.detail: 61 units, ~9 of them net-new engines + dispatcher actions at 1.5x and 1-3/day -> ~3.5 single-lane dev-weeks even though raw count suggests 1 week. Treat the 9 backend-prereq + 5 net-new engine units as a serialized sub-critical-path; the 37 customer pages parallelize cheaply behind them.
findings.recommendation: Lock SFC GA date to backend-prereq completion + 1 wk page-wiring, not to total unit count.

findings.title: MS3 wire-backlog must not be on the GA critical path
findings.detail: Round-4 finding: 531 true-revenue-relevant orphans, only 116 wired in MS3's 12 batches @ 9.5 avg, 415 deferred to MS3.5, 289 ML-plumbing deferred. At 9.5 units/batch and ~1 batch/day that is ~12 working days for MS3 alone; MS3.5's 415 is ~6-7 dev-weeks. If GA gates on MS3.5 the ship date slips a quarter.
findings.recommendation: GA gates on MS3 (116 wired) only. MS3.5 (415) runs post-GA as continuous background lane.

findings.title: Master Post GA depends on MS0 + MS3-Lathe + dialect coverage units, not standalone
findings.detail: Post-processor GA needs SpindleCharacteristicEngine (MS0 P0), the Lathe wire batches BATCH12-15 (MS3), and the 5-dialect coverage units. Earliest realistic = after MS0 backend-prereq + Lathe batches land = ~wk 9-10 single-lane / ~wk 6-7 calendar.
findings.recommendation: Sequence Master Post GA strictly after MS3 Lathe batches; do not promise it concurrent with SFC GA.

findings.title: MS-PILOT phase-7 is per-machine and must be priced per-unit not as one milestone
findings.detail: phase-7 (machine hardening / first-part-right validation) repeats per machine. JM Die has 21 ShopConfig machines; even if pilot scopes to ~5 priority machines that is 5 x ~1.5-2 dev-weeks = 7.5-10 dev-weeks. Cannot land before MS-TRAIN (LoRA/per-machine calibration) completes.
findings.recommendation: Roadmap should show MS-PILOT-P7 as N sub-units (one per pilot machine) with explicit MS-TRAIN dependency edge.

findings.title: P2 multiplier (0.7x) is optimistic for viz/wiki-style units
findings.detail: Recent U-VIZ-* commits show wiki/crosslink units actually run faster than 0.7x (638 skills + 483 hooks in one commit) — but only because they are batch-generated. Hand-authored P2 units (UI polish, docs) run at ~1.0x. Bimodal: keep 0.7x only for generator-backed units, use 1.0x for hand work.
findings.recommendation: Split P2 into P2-gen (0.6x) and P2-hand (1.0x) in the build-cost model.

MS0_SFC.notes: 9 backend-prereq + 5 net-new engine (P0 1.5x, 1-3/day) dominate; 37 pages parallelize cheap

MS3_wire_core.notes: 12 batches @ 9.5 engines avg; ~1 batch/day under 3way scrutiny

MS3_5_wire_backlog.notes: POST-GA continuous lane; NOT on critical path

SFC_GA.gate: MS0 backend-prereq + 5 net-new engines + page-wiring; NOT MS3.5

Master_Post_GA.gate: after MS0 + MS3 Lathe BATCH12-15 + 5-dialect coverage

gantt_sequencing_recommendation: WK1-4  | MS0 backend-prereq (serial, P0) ────────► then MS0 37 pages (parallel) | START: SpindleCharacteristicEngine, ToolCatalogEngine first
WK2-4  | MS1 + MS2 (parallel lane, behind MS0 dispatcher actions landing)
WK4-7  | MS3 core: 12 wire batches, Lathe-first (BATCH12,13,TURNING1,14,15 then Machine/Multi/Other) — 1 batch/day under 3way scrutiny
WK6-8  | MS_MASTERPOST: skeleton (needs MS0 spindle engine) || 5-dialect coverage (needs MS3 Lathe batches) — overlap tail of MS3
WK9-10 | ★ Master Post GA milestone gate
WK10-13| MS_PILOT: phases 1-6 (1 calendar wk) then phase-7 PER MACHINE x5 (1.5-2 dev-wk each, can 2-up if machines independent)
WK10+  | MS3.5 (415 engines) + MS-ML-PLUMBING (289) — CONTINUOUS BACKGROUND LANE, never blocks a GA gate
WK13   | ★ MS-PILOT phase-7 first 5 machines complete → pilot-ready
RULE   | P0 units NEVER parallelize across chats (shared dispatcher + scrutiny gate). P1/P2 fan out to all 6 chats freely.

consensus_signal: AGREE-WITH-CAVEAT: v7.1's ~215-unit / 9-milestone structure is shippable in ~10 calendar weeks ONLY if (1) MS3.5's 415-engine wire-backlog is explicitly OFF the GA critical path, (2) MS0 backend-prereq + 5 net-new engines are serialized as a sub-critical-path priced at 1-3 units/day not 6, and (3) MS-PILOT phase-7 is decomposed into per-machine sub-units with a hard MS-TRAIN dependency edge. Without those three corrections the implied dates slip by ~1 quarter. Aligns with round-4 finding that the old 47-engine-per-batch MS3 was 7.8x overloaded — the corrected 9.5/batch cadence is the right anchor.
